target: Conclusion: '20 bps is about parity with Ren at MS GIFT' and 'a market price for programs averaging $250k+' (01-pricing-and-scope.md:7-14; PRC summary/(e))
defect_or_objection: Parity holds only near MS GIFT's own balance (~$371-399k avg). At the top-25 hypothesis sponsors (median avg balance ~$1.1M) 20 bps = $2,221 per account-year, 3.0x Ren's $737 at MS GIFT and 2.7x the top of the observed staffed band ($815). Per-account price, not bps, is the stable market quantity (PRC (b)), so the higher the balance the further 20 bps sits ABOVE market.
magnitude: If buyers pay the lesser of 20 bps or $737/account, sponsors that alone cover Model B fixed ($1.74M) fall from 20 to 5; at $400/account to 2
fix_or_test: Re-express every offer as $/account-year plus a declining bps tier; rerun sponsor CSV with min(bps fee, per-account cap); test acceptance in design-partner conversations

target: Integrator 02 conclusion 2: '20 sponsors could alone cover the lean organization's fixed cost'
defect_or_objection: Count assumes 20 bps on multi-$B, high-balance books. Of the 5 that survive a per-account cap of $737: NPT is a competitor, AEF migrated to Ren in 2026, Greater Horizons is a GKCCF affiliate (same buying decision). Realistic single-sponsor sustainers: about 2 decision units (JCF, GKCCF group).
magnitude: 20 -> 5 -> ~2 decision units
fix_or_test: Replace with count under per-account cap and exclusions; publish both

target: research/commercial-opportunity/servicing-economics/model/src/ServicingEconomics/Strategies.fs:70 (Approach = AiNative for every plan from go-live)
defect_or_objection: AI-native minutes are applied from the first live month although Unbound EV-08 says up to eight sponsor-side authorisations (board delegation, auditor approach, bank agreements, controller policies) must exist first and 'until then the sponsor operates near C0'; ACT RC-ACT-007 says the servicer cannot reach redesigned cost until delegation exists.

fix_or_test: Make Approach a function of months since each sponsor's go-live and of a delegation date; base case AI-enhanced for 12 months, AI-native only after a measured time study

defect_or_objection: Platform build is costed only as $60k/month for 12 months ($0.72M) of contract engineering in the cash plans and is absent from every annual break-even/margin table (results.md header says 'before platform build amortisation'). Unbound's own vendor model assumes $5M ($3-15M) build capex; ECH says the 2-engineer core presumes a platform that does not exist.
magnitude: Break-even (5 sponsors, $150k, 20 bps) $1.97B -> $2.06B with $0.72M/5y, -> $2.87B with $5M/5y
fix_or_test: Add a platform amortisation or internal licence line to fixed cost; show tables with and without it

target: research/commercial-opportunity/servicing-economics/model/src/ServicingEconomics/Parameters.fs:166 and CST Model B sales line ($42k) / Strategies.fs:109

defect_or_objection: Added staff capacity uses 1,520 productive hours as fully available queue time. ACT sizes hires at 1,360 queue hours (1,600 x 0.85 utilisation). No utilisation factor in the F# model.
magnitude: 5 sponsors $1.5B $150k: added FTE 6 -> 7, profit -$560k -> -$670k; break-even $1.97B -> $2.04B
fix_or_test: Add a utilisation parameter (0.85-0.9) applied to added and core servicing hours

defect_or_objection: December overflow is bought at the full loaded rate although annual added FTE are already sized to include those hours (overflow hours are paid twice in money terms). At the same time the rule assumes fungible hours: CST-P14 says temps 'can only prepare, not release', RC-ACT-002 makes surge reviewers sponsor-exclusive, and peak week runs ~8x average daily (ACT-9), which a monthly bucket cannot see.
magnitude: Peak cost $97.9k at 5 sponsors/$1.5B (3.3% of revenue) is the double-count bound; the structural understatement is a per-sponsor pre-qualified releaser bench (not modelled)
fix_or_test: Size base staff to non-December load, model December as (a) preparers at temp rate and (b) a per-sponsor releaser bench as step-fixed; add a peak-week queue test

defect_or_objection: Compliance-officer step is triggered by average assets > $1B, so a market fall fires the compliance officer: total cost falls $121,848 in the -40%/-50% stresses (results.md Model B stress table: $3.56M -> $3.44M). Cost is non-monotone in a downturn.
magnitude: $122k/yr in severe stresses
fix_or_test: Trigger on accounts/sponsors or ratchet (hire-once); add a property test: cost must not fall when only AssetFactor falls

defect_or_objection: Every sponsor gets the same 20/20/40/7/10/3% archetype mix with balances scaled to its average and workload held constant. Results: SVCF ($8.4M avg) breaks even at 0.2 bps because a $57M 'high-value' account costs the same as a $3M one; at $75k-average programs 'small recurring' accounts hold $1,368 and 'complex-asset' accounts $256k yet still incur $358/yr intermediary fees.
effect_direction: overstates high-balance attractiveness; overstates cost at low-balance programs
magnitude: Drives the top of the sponsor ranking (break-even <1 bps at SVCF, NPT, GS DAPF, CCT)
fix_or_test: Segment-specific mixes; workload that rises with balance band (grants, wires, complex gifts); validate with any sponsor's balance distribution

defect_or_objection: Per-sponsor 'marginal contribution' used for the 1,540-row CSV excludes step costs that are per-sponsor in nature (integration engineer and implementation analyst per 8 sponsors = ~$39.5k per sponsor-year; fund accountant ~$7.38/account; ops-manager uplift ~25% on added labour; December peak), but charges every hour at the marginal rate although ~3,268 h/yr are already paid in fixed cost (core servicing share + the minimum added FTE that is also inside modelBFixed).
effect_direction: small sponsors overstated; first/anchor sponsor understated
magnitude: ~$40-60k/yr per small sponsor overstated; up to ~$214k understated for the first sponsor
fix_or_test: Report allocated contribution (steps allocated by driver) alongside marginal; define 'covers fixed alone' as standalone P&L of a one-sponsor company

defect_or_objection: 'Net outflow -15% assets' is an AssetFactor only. If the outflow is grant payout, grant volume rises while revenue falls (the payout-revenue scissors); no VolumeFactor is applied.
magnitude: Not quantified; volume x1.15-1.3 alongside -15% assets
fix_or_test: Pair outflow stress with a payout-linked VolumeFactor

defect_or_objection: Concentration is stressed only on five equal sponsors (largest = 20% of AUA). The recommended anchor plan has the anchor at 60% of AUA. Without it the remaining $1.0B book runs at -$239k/yr; anchor alone after a 30% market fall runs at -$156k.
magnitude: Run-rate profit $1.78M -> -$0.24M if anchor lost

defect_or_objection: Strategy comparison is confounded: the plans differ in total AUA (C $2.5B, D $1.8B, B $1.5B, E $1.2B) and in average balance (anchor $300k; others $200k; partner $150k). The ranking mostly reflects those inputs, not the entry route.
magnitude: C with anchor at $200k: run-rate $1.54M vs $1.78M; D at $300k: $0.60M vs $0.09M

defect_or_objection: Partnership plan nets 14 bps at $150k balances with no implementation fee and no CAC credit; wealth-channel partners are where Ren/TIFIN/bank affiliates are entrenched and where advisory economics (60-100 bps) dominate.
magnitude: Plan E loses -$1.07M/yr run-rate; result driven by 14 bps x $150k, not by partnership

defect_or_objection: Revenue starts at full steady-state AUA in the go-live month: no migration ramp, no asset growth or attrition, no churn, no renegotiation at renewal, no market path.

defect_or_objection: 'Capital required' is the cash trough including 10% interest on negative balances, mixing an equity need with debt cost.
magnitude: Roughly the cumulative interest, order $0.2-0.3M on the anchor plan [E]

defect_or_objection: Annual December peak cost is spread evenly over 12 months, so December cash outflow is understated and other months overstated.
magnitude: <$0.1M timing

defect_or_objection: '20 bps + $250 per-account floor' is not a 20 bps price: effective 30.3 bps at $150k-average and 44.7 bps at $75k-average books. Because the floor applies to rescaled archetype balances, $1,368 'small recurring' funds pay $250/yr (18% of balance) and $3,420 inactive funds 7.3%.
fix_or_test: Always print effective bps and $/account; cap floor at a % of balance; exempt dormant funds under a sweep policy

defect_or_objection: Per-account floor is evaluated on archetype averages (max of average, not average of max). With dispersion inside an archetype more accounts fall below the floor than modelled.
effect_direction: floor revenue and donor burden understated

defect_or_objection: Base case charges payment rails (~$25.6/account mix) and complex-asset intermediary fees ($350/gift, ~$10.8/account mix) to the servicer although CST says rails are sponsor pass-through when the sponsor's bank originates and ACT says intermediary fees are often fund-borne. defect_or_objection: No exceptional-service or activity fees although the market charges them (MS GIFT $2,000-3,500 per grant to other grantee categories, 2019 circular; RCF foreign/509(a)(3)/event fees) and ACT shows 20% of accounts drive ~60% of AI-native minutes.
magnitude: Not quantified
fix_or_test: Add an activity fee schedule for complex gifts, foreign/ER grants, wires

defect_or_objection: Activity PassThrough flag removes cost unconditionally and is never billed; not tied to price.PaymentsPassThrough. No current activity sets it, so latent.

defect_or_objection: Controller's 456 h/yr count as servicing (preparation) capacity although the controller is the reviewer; ACT/budget forbid self-review. Same pattern in Model A (controller 0.3).

target: Integrator 02 conclusions 2-4; SPN top-25 and self-sustaining lists
defect_or_objection: At community-foundation and national targets a 20 bps fee equals a median 11% (top-25) and 20% (self-sustaining list) of the sponsor's ENTIRE non-investment operating cost (programs, development, community grantmaking included). Examples with own staff: JCF 71% (25 employees), Greater Horizons 90%, GiveWell CF 85%, Independent Charitable Gift Fund 77%. A fee that large is unlikely to be below the sponsor's avoided DAF-admin cost. Unbound EV-04 already rejected CFs as the entry segment.
magnitude: Applies to most of the top-25
fix_or_test: For each target compute avoided cost from 990 Part IX staff lines x DAF share; interview to test

defect_or_objection: Anchor ($1.5B, 5,000 accounts, $300k average) signs at month 12 and goes live at month 18 with no evidence that such a buyer exists, is in a renewal window, or will migrate in 6 months; onboarding cost is the flat $105k used for a $20M sponsor.
magnitude: +6 months adds $0.77M capital; no-anchor case has no trough bound
fix_or_test: Gate capital tranches to signed LOI; scale onboarding by accounts and feeds (CST range $35-325k)

target: PRC (a),(e): Ren at MS GIFT as 'anchor comparable'
defect_or_objection: MS GIFT is a 0-employee bank-channel program: Ren's 18.5 bps ('ADMIN & LEGAL') sits beside MSSB's separate 7 bps platform/administration fee and up to 3 bps sponsor GOE, so total administration economics there are ~25-28 bps; and the sponsor retains almost nothing, whereas this offer leaves reserved decisions (~$42-43/fund) with the sponsor. 'Parity' is ill-defined in both directions.
magnitude: Comparator could be 18.5 or ~25.5 bps depending on scope

defect_or_objection: Ren's MS GIFT price is set inside a channel relationship at $9.1B / 21,800 accounts where the channel earns 60-100 bps advisory; it is not an arm's-length price an entrant at $0.5-1.5B can obtain or must beat.
magnitude: n/a
fix_or_test: Use arm's-length observations (USCGT, Stifel stack, TIFIN list) as the entrant band

defect_or_objection: Asset-based fees reward retention: the servicer earns less when payout rises while workload rises; the per-account floor rewards keeping many small/dormant funds open; ACT's December deferral (grant SLA up to 10 business days) saves servicer cost by delaying grants; complex gifts carry $358 + 359 min cost with no activity fee, an incentive to discourage them. No safeguard is modelled.
magnitude: Money incentive to delay a $10k grant 30 days is ~$1.64 (small); the cost incentive (staffing) and retention incentive (fee base) are large
fix_or_test: Adopt safeguards in ADV-14; report payout-neutrality metrics

target: ACT-4, ECH-1: redesign levers as the advantage
